entries.title: II Samuel 19:2
segments: Excessive sorrow unfits the soul for duty, displeases God, and tends to injure all who indulge it or feel its influence.

entries.title: II Samuel 19:3
segments: Gat them by stealth; secretly, privately, because the king appeared as if he was displeased at what they had done.

entries.title: II Samuel 19:6
segments:
Thou lovest thine enemies; Joab's meaning was, that David by so mourning for Absalom acted as if he loved him more than he did his family and people, whose lives had been saved by the death of Absalom. 
 
Rulers, as well as people, should be plainly told of their duty, and such motives set before them as are suited to induce them to perform it.

entries.title: II Samuel 19:7
segments: Speak comfortably unto thy servants; show thyself pleased with their victory.

entries.title: II Samuel 19:8
segments: The approbation of rulers should be promptly and cheerfully given to those who do right, and their disapprobation manifested towards those who do wrong.

entries.title: II Samuel 19:11
segments:
The speech of all Israel is come; expressing their desire to have the king return. 
 
All prudent care should be taken to avoid coming evils, especially to prevent discord among brethren, and to lead them to cooperate for the public good.

entries.title: II Samuel 19:12
segments: My flesh; of the same tribe with him.

entries.title: II Samuel 19:13
segments: Amasa; he had been the commander of Absalom's army.
When men are strongly excited and set upon accomplishing a favorite object, they are tempted to make rash promises, and to adopt measures which events show to have been unwise.

entries.title: II Samuel 19:14
segments: He bowed the heart of all the men of Judah; according to some, Amasa did this; but others understand David as doing it through his messages to Zadok and Abiathar.

entries.title: II Samuel 19:19
segments: Thy servant did perversely;

If men confess their sins and appear to be penitent, it is ordinarily wise to treat them as if they were so.  God alone knows the heart, and men ought not to judge of it, except so far as its character is manifested in the conduct.

entries.title: II Samuel 19:23
segments: Not die; not be put to death for that offence.

entries.title: II Samuel 19:24
segments:
Neither dressed--nor trimmed--nor washed; showing that he had been in a state of deep mourning ever since David left the city. 
 
True love will show itself in grief at the sorrows of those beloved, and in joy at the return of their joys.

entries.title: II Samuel 19:26
segments: My servant; Ziba.

entries.title: II Samuel 19:27
segments: Slandered thy servant;
Slander is a common and aggravated sin, and the slanderer, though he often escape punishment from men, is and ought to be regarded as among the basest of sinners.

entries.title: II Samuel 19:29
segments: Divide the land; the land that had belonged to Saul, and which David, after restoring it to Mephibosheth, had hastily given to Ziba.

entries.title: II Samuel 19:31
segments: Barzillai;

entries.title: II Samuel 19:32
segments: Kindness and active benevolence are peculiarly agreeable in the aged, and should ever be met with grateful and active kindness in return.  As their tastes for the comforts of this life are diminishing, their desires for those of the future should be increasing, and their chief concern be for preparation to close their work on earth, and enter the rest of heaven.

entries.title: II Samuel 19:37
segments: Chimham; he seems to have been the son of Barzillai.
Aged benevolent men are pleased to have those who are younger partake of lawful innocent enjoyments, for which they themselves have no relish.

entries.title: II Samuel 19:38
segments: The kindness and fidelity of parents the Lord often rewards in blessings on their children and children's children; thus showing mercy even to thousands of those who love him and keep his commandments.

entries.title: II Samuel 19:41
segments: Stolen thee away; gone first and brought the king without consulting the other tribes.

entries.title: II Samuel 19:42
segments: Near of kin; he belonged to their tribe.
